newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends surge to hit eight-month high.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends surge to hit eight-month high.

text.p: The ringgit rebounded quickly after a brief consolidation against the dollar, surging to an eight-month high on renewed speculative demand on Thursday, dealers said.
"The (ringgit) uptrend is still intact," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the ringgit may be heading higher as fundamentals and confidence in the Malaysian unit prevailed.
Dealers said the ringgit jumped about 100 points from its Kuala Lumpur morning low.
At 0600 GMT, the ringgit was trading at 2.4838/48 a dollar.
The ringgit closed in Kuala Lumpur at 2.4877/87.
The ringgit had earlier succumbed to pressure from dollar short-covering and strong demand for dollar/yen.
But the setback was widely seen as temporary, given the strong speculative demand for ringgit.

Dealers said a news report which quoted Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar as saying the government was comfortable with recent strengthening of the ringgit may also have contributed to the surge.
